turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hi, I'm Rita, an MSc student. My thesis topic was just approved: 'misinformation in Portuguese news'. My supervisor, Prof. Almeida, says it's far too broad. Can you help me plan it?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Of course. 'Misinformation in Portuguese news' could be a whole research group's agenda, so the first job is narrowing it to something you can finish in one MSc. We'll plan the thesis in stages: scope, research questions, data, method, then writing.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How would you narrow it?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Pick one kind of misinformation. Health claims are a good candidate: there was a huge amount of it in Portuguese media during COVID, fact-checkers labelled much of it, and the harm is concrete.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I like that. Health claims it is.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Great. The thesis is now about misleading health claims in Portuguese news.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Next: what makes a good research question?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: One you can answer with the data and time you have, whose answer isn't already known, and that is specific enough to tell whether you answered it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you give examples for my topic?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A feasibility question ('can current models detect misleading health claims in Portuguese news, and how well?') and a comparison question, for instance about the two main varieties of Portuguese, where resources are very unequal.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then my RQs are: RQ1, can models detect misleading health claims in Portuguese news? RQ2, does performance differ between European and Brazilian Portuguese?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Those are clear and answerable. RQ1 is feasibility, RQ2 is the variety comparison. Write them at the top of your thesis document; everything else should serve them.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I met Prof. Almeida. He liked both RQs, but told me to keep the focus on European Portuguese, since that's the gap.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Makes sense: PT-BR has far more resources, so PT-PT is where a contribution is most needed.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So I limit the scope to European Portuguese news only?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes: scope limited to PT-PT news. RQ2 can still use PT-BR material as a point of comparison later if needed.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Which Portuguese outlets should I collect from?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Pick outlets that fact-checkers cover, so you can get labels.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Which ones do fact-checkers cover most?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Público, Observador, Expresso and Jornal de Notícias, plus claims the fact-checker Polígrafo has already rated, which gives you labels for free.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Many 2020–2021 articles are gone from the sites. How do I get older ones?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Arquivo.pt, the Portuguese web archive, has most of them, and it has an API for bulk access.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, and the submission deadline is 30 June.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Then we have about 21 weeks. Let's plan backwards: data by mid-April, experiments by the end of May, writing in June.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Starting the literature review. Where do I begin?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: With claim detection, the task your RQ1 is about.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What's the core literature on claim detection?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: The CheckThat! lab series is the anchor: claim-worthiness detection and verification tasks, several languages, strong baselines to cite.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I also cover full fact-checking pipelines, with evidence retrieval and verdicts?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Briefly, to position your work: you do detection, not verification. One section is enough.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Second strand: health misinformation specifically.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Health misinformation datasets and studies, especially COVID-era ones. This strand justifies the focus you chose in RQ1.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Are there Portuguese-specific resources?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Let's check what exists for each variety.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What did you find?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Very little for PT-PT. For PT-BR there's the Fake.br corpus and the BERTimbau language model, which is trained on Brazilian Portuguese but often used for both.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Third strand: using LLMs directly as classifiers.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Zero-shot and few-shot classification with instruction-tuned LLMs, a fast-growing literature, with mixed results on non-English data.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do they work for Portuguese?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Decently for PT-BR, largely untested for PT-PT. That's another gap your thesis sits in.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I found FakeRecogna: a labelled fake-news dataset in Portuguese, including health. But it's all Brazilian.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Useful, but only PT-BR.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you summarise the literature so far?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Three strands: claim detection (CheckThat!), health misinformation (datasets and studies), and LLMs as classifiers. Across all three, PT-PT is the gap.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I use FakeRecogna even though my scope is PT-PT?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Not as your main data. It's Brazilian, and your scope is PT-PT only.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then I'll build my own PT-PT dataset: at least 2,000 annotated health claims.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Ambitious but valuable: it would be the first PT-PT resource of its kind. Plan the annotation carefully, since it will be the slowest part.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How should I set up the annotation?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Write guidelines first: what counts as a health claim, what counts as misleading, with examples.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And to show the labels are reliable?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A second annotator on a subset. Your colleague Duarte could double-annotate part of the data, and you report Cohen's kappa for agreement.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: For the model, I'll fine-tune BERTimbau as my main method.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A reasonable default: it's the standard Portuguese encoder, and fine-tuning is well understood.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What hyperparameters should I start with?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Learning rate 2e-5, batch size 16, 3–4 epochs, and early stopping on a validation split.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Base or large model?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: BERTimbau-large usually scores a few points higher, but needs much more GPU memory and time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The only GPU I can use is the faculty server: one 16 GB card, shared.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's a hard limit. 16 GB is tight for BERTimbau-large even with small batches.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Annotation update: in three weeks, Duarte and I have annotated 180 claims.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's about 60 a week. Let's see what that means for the 2,000 target.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How long would 2,000 take at this rate?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: About 33 weeks. That's well past 30 June.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I tried BERTimbau-large on the server: out of memory, even at batch size 4.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: As feared. 16 GB isn't enough for large.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And BERTimbau-base fits, but on my 180 claims it's barely above chance.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: With so few labelled examples, base underfits. Fine-tuning needs far more data than you'll have.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm worried. Where does this leave the plan?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Two problems at once: the annotation pace [N_31] makes 2,000 claims impossible by June, and the GPU limit [N_33] makes fine-tuning large models impossible. The plan needs to change.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So I drop fine-tuning as the main method?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes. Drop fine-tuning BERTimbau as the main method: it can't work with this data and this hardware.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What replaces it?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Zero-shot and few-shot classification with an LLM through an API (GPT-4o-mini, for example). It needs no training data beyond a few examples and no GPU of your own.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: But doesn't that weaken the thesis? Anyone can call an API.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: The novelty was never the model. It's the PT-PT question: whether classifiers built on Brazilian data work on European Portuguese. That question stays, and an LLM makes it easier to test.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And the 2,000-claim dataset? Honestly, it's not going to happen.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Agreed. Abandon the 2,000-claim goal; the time is better spent on experiments.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then what data do I use?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: FakeRecogna for few-shot examples and development, and your own annotated PT-PT claims, topped up to 400, as the test set. 400 is reachable in a few more weeks.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: But FakeRecogna is Brazilian, and my scope is PT-PT only.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Then the scope has to widen: include both PT-PT and PT-BR. Without PT-BR data, there's nothing to learn from.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Does RQ2 still make sense then?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: It gets sharper. Reframe RQ2 as a transfer question: how well does a classifier built with PT-BR data and examples work on PT-PT news? That's exactly what FakeRecogna plus your 400 PT-PT claims can answer.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Let me make sure I have the new plan straight.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Method: LLM zero/few-shot [N_37]. Data: FakeRecogna plus 400 own PT-PT claims [N_40]. RQ2: transfer from PT-BR to PT-PT [N_42]. Scope: both varieties.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: With only two annotators, is my annotation reliable enough to report?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: It can be, if the agreement is good; that's what the kappa will tell us.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How many claims should we both annotate for the kappa?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Around 100 of the 400, sampled at random, annotated independently before you compare.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How should I design the zero-shot prompt?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Give the model a precise definition of a misleading health claim and a fixed label set, and ask for the label only.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should the definition come from my annotation guidelines?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes, use exactly the guideline definitions, so the model and the annotators apply the same criteria.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: For few-shot, how do I pick the examples?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Balanced across labels, and short.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: From which data, though?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: From FakeRecogna (PT-BR), testing on your PT-PT claims. That makes the few-shot setting itself a test of RQ2's transfer question.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: First results with GPT-4o-mini on the PT-PT test set: zero-shot macro-F1 0.61, few-shot 0.68. Just in time for my midterm presentation next week.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good first numbers to present: few-shot helps by 7 points even with Brazilian examples.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is 0.68 actually good?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: For a hard, subjective task with no PT-PT training data it's respectable; CheckThat! systems on similar tasks land in the 0.6–0.8 range.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Duarte and I finished the 100 double-annotated claims: kappa is 0.71.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: 0.71 is 'substantial' agreement on the usual scale. The annotation is reliable enough to report.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Meeting with Prof. Almeida. He says having no fine-tuned baseline at all is a red flag for any examiner.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: He has a point: without a trained baseline, examiners can't tell whether the LLM is actually good or just the only thing tried.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: But we dropped fine-tuning because it didn't fit on the GPU!

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: BERTimbau-large didn't fit. A smaller multilingual model would, and it only needs to be a baseline, not the main method.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Which model then?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: XLM-R-base: multilingual, fits comfortably on 16 GB, and fine-tuned on FakeRecogna it gives a proper trained baseline. The LLM stays the main method, compared against XLM-R.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: XLM-R results: fine-tuned on FakeRecogna, it gets 0.64 macro-F1 on held-out PT-BR data.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: 0.64 in-variety is a solid baseline.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And on the PT-PT test set it drops to 0.52.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A 12-point drop across varieties. That's a clear transfer gap, exactly what RQ2 asks about, and the LLM's 0.68 holds up much better.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I replace GPT-4o-mini with Llama-3.1-8B running locally, for reproducibility?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Worth considering: API models change without notice.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What are the trade-offs?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Llama is fully reproducible and free, but will likely score lower; GPT-4o-mini scores higher but may change or disappear. Reporting only one hides something either way.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Prof. Almeida suggested also submitting a short paper to PROPOR 2026. Should I?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A paper would strengthen your CV, and the transfer result is publishable. Let's plan for it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: When is the PROPOR deadline?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: 20 June, so ten days before your thesis deadline.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: On the Llama question: can I just report both?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes, report both. GPT-4o-mini as the main result and Llama-3.1-8B as the reproducible reference; the gap between them is itself informative.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm behind. The error analysis isn't started and there's a month left before 30 June.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's tight for experiments, error analysis and writing.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good news: the faculty approved my extension request. The new deadline is 15 September.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That changes everything: the deadline is now 15 September, which leaves room for a proper error analysis.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I still try for the PROPOR paper?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: The paper deadline is 20 June regardless of your extension. Writing it now would take the time the extension just gave you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then I'll skip PROPOR and focus on the thesis.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Sensible. You can turn the thesis into a paper for a later venue once it's submitted.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Starting the error analysis. Where does the transfer from PT-BR to PT-PT fail most?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Look at the PT-PT claims that XLM-R gets wrong but classifies correctly on similar PT-BR items.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A lot of errors involve vocabulary and idioms that differ between the varieties.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's a classic variety effect: everyday words and set phrases differ enough to confuse a model trained on Brazilian text.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And institution names: claims about the SNS and the DGS get misclassified much more than claims about the SUS and Anvisa.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Health institutions are country-specific (Portugal's SNS and DGS vs Brazil's SUS and Anvisa), so claims about them look unfamiliar to a PT-BR-trained model.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How should I present the error analysis?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Group errors into categories (vocabulary, institutions, other), give counts per category, and two or three examples each.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Time to plan the writing. What structure?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Six chapters: introduction, related work, data, method, results and error analysis, conclusions. Keep related work before method, so the reader knows the gap before seeing your approach.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What goes into the method chapter?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: The models, the prompts and the evaluation protocol.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Which models exactly, and in what role?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: GPT-4o-mini and Llama-3.1-8B as the zero/few-shot classifiers, XLM-R-base as the fine-tuned baseline, and macro-F1 on the 400 PT-PT claims as the main metric.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Writing the introduction, I realised I'm not sure what my RQs are anymore. What were they, and do they still match what I did?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: You set them back in February [N_6] and changed RQ2 in April [N_42]; let's check them against the current work.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So what do I write?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: RQ1 is unchanged: can models detect misleading health claims in Portuguese news. RQ2 is now the transfer question: how well does a classifier built on PT-BR work on PT-PT. The introduction has to explain that pivot honestly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What goes in the limitations section?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Three things: the small test set, since the 2,000-claim dataset was abandoned [N_39]; only two annotators, though with kappa 0.71 [N_52]; and the single 16 GB GPU [N_30], which ruled out large fine-tuned models.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you summarise every change of plan, so the story in the thesis is honest?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Four pivots: fine-tuning was dropped as the main method [N_36]; the scope widened from PT-PT to both varieties [N_41]; a fine-tuned XLM-R baseline came back at the supervisor's request [N_55]; and the PROPOR paper was dropped after the extension [N_66].

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I sent chapters 1–3 to Prof. Almeida.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good. Keep writing the results chapter while he reads.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He's happy with them. His only comment: tighten the evaluation chapter.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's a good position to be in by the end of June, with more than two months until the deadline.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I submitted the thesis today, four days before the 15 September deadline!

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Congratulations, Rita! From 'misinformation in Portuguese news' to a submitted thesis with a real transfer finding.
